behaviours.title: A deposit increases the balance by the deposited amount
behaviours.then: the deposit is accepted and the balance is 10

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); const r = l.deposit('a', 10, 't1');

behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused and the balance stays 0

behaviours.title: A withdrawal larger than the balance is rejected
behaviours.then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'insufficient-funds' and the balance stays 100

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); l.deposit('a', 100, 't1'); const r = l.withdraw('a', 150, 't2');

behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -50

behaviours.title: Withdrawals are capped at 5000 per account
behaviours.given: an account with balance 10000 that has already withdrawn 4000
behaviours.then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 6000

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); l.deposit('a', 10000, 't1'); l.withdraw('a', 4000, 't2'); const r = l.withdraw('a', 1500, 't3');

behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted; there is no limit

behaviours.title: Amounts are rounded half-up to two decimal places
A repeated transaction id is acknowledged and has no effect, even with a different amount
behaviours.given: an account where 50 was deposited with transaction id 't1'
behaviours.when: 70 is deposited again with transaction id 't1'
behaviours.then: the call reports success and the balance stays 50

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); l.deposit('a', 50, 't1'); const r = l.deposit('a', 70, 't1');

behaviours.contrary_then: the second call is rejected because its amount differs from the first call with the same id

behaviours.title: A non-positive amount is rejected
behaviours.then: the operation is rejected with reason 'invalid-amount'

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); const r = l.withdraw('a', 0, 't1'); const r2 = l.transfer('a', 'b', -5, 't2');
test.assert: expect(r).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }); expect(r2).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' });

behaviours.contrary_then: a zero amount is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: A transfer moves the amount and records an entry on both accounts
behaviours.given: account 'a' with balance 100 and an empty account 'b'
behaviours.then: 'a' has 60, 'b' has 40, and each history has one new entry with the same transaction id

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); l.deposit('a', 100, 't1'); l.transfer('a', 'b', 40, 't2');
test.assert: expect(l.balance('a')).toBe(60); expect(l.balance('b')).toBe(40); expect(l.entries('a').at(-1)).toEqual({ txnId: 't2', kind: 'transfer-out', amount: 40 }); expect(l.entries('b')).toEqual([{ txnId: 't2', kind: 'transfer-in', amount: 40 }]);

behaviours.contrary_then: the amount leaves 'a' but does not arrive in 'b'

behaviours.title: The balance of an unknown account is 0
behaviours.then: the result is 0 and no error is raised
behaviours.contrary_then: reading an unknown account raises an error

behaviours.title: (deliberately vacuous, to show the twin check) deposits succeed

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); const r = l.deposit('a', 5, 't1');

behaviours.title: (deliberately wrong, to show refutation) the limit resets after each withdrawal

test.arrange_act: const l = new Ledger(); l.deposit('a', 9000, 't1'); l.withdraw('a', 5000, 't2'); const r = l.withdraw('a', 1, 't3');
